Compare validation and target nearest-neighbour distances

Source: R/contrasts.R
distance_contrasts.Rd

Calculates exact integrals for weighted empirical distributions, without a numerical integration grid. A is mean target distance minus mean validation distance; W is their one-dimensional Wasserstein distance. J1 and J2 are validation minus target averages of correlation and squared correlation. U1 and U2 are Wasserstein distances between those transformed values.

Usage

distance_contrasts(
  validation,
  target,
  correlation = NULL,
  validation_weights = NULL,
  target_weights = NULL
)

Arguments

validation, target

Nonempty numeric vectors of finite, nonnegative nearest-training distances.

correlation

A function mapping distances to correlations in [-1, 1], or a spatial_covariance() object. If NULL, correlation diagnostics are NA.

validation_weights, target_weights

Nonnegative weights, normalised separately. Defaults are equal weights within each distribution.

Value

A named numeric vector: A, W, J1, J2, U1, U2, Aplus, Aminus, and crosses (one if both positive and negative CDF areas exceed a relative floating-point tolerance, otherwise zero).

Details

A positive J2 means higher average squared nearest-observation correlation during validation. Under Gaussian prediction using one neighbour with known mean and covariance, target MSE minus expected CV MSE equals total variance times J2. This is not a general bias correction for fitted prediction models. The integral interpretation of U1 and U2 as unsigned weighted distance-CDF contrasts assumes nonnegative correlation decreasing with distance.

Examples

model <- spatial_covariance(range = 1, signal = 0.8)
distance_contrasts(c(0.2, 0.5, 1), c(0.5, 1, 2), model)
#>         A         W        J1        J2        U1        U2     Aplus    Aminus 
#> 0.6000000 0.6000000 0.1822388 0.1390943 0.1822388 0.1390943 0.6000000 0.0000000 
#>   crosses 
#> 0.0000000
